title: Expression and block bodies: discount and categorize prices

blocks.text: A lambda is a parameter list, the arrow `->`, and a body. The body is either a single expression, `(parameters) -> expression`, or a block of statements, `(parameters) -> { statements; }`, which may declare local variables and branch.
Write two static methods in `PriceRules`, each mapping a lambda over the prices:

items: `discounted(List<Double> prices, double percent)` returns each price reduced by `percent` per cent (which may have a fraction, like `12.5`). The final price, not the discount, is rounded to the nearest cent with `Math.round` (a half cent rounds up), even when `percent` is 0.
`categorize(List<Double> prices)` names each price's band: below 10 is `"cheap"` (0 included), below 100 `"moderate"`, below 1000 `"expensive"`, and anything else `"premium"`.

blocks.text: Watch the prices that sit exactly on a limit, and what floating-point arithmetic leaves after a percentage.

cases.says: Each price is reduced by the given percentage.
Prices well inside each band get that band's category.
A discounted price is rounded to two decimal places.
A price exactly on a limit (10, 100, 1000) belongs to the higher category.
A price is rounded to the nearest cent, so 2.997 becomes 3.0; cutting off the extra digits is not rounding.

concepts: A lambda is a parameter list, the arrow, and a body that is one expression or a block of statements.
